text:
jamie: Escalation from ACME on Private VPC — lots of client SDK TLS failures after last cert rotation (saw spike ~2026-03-16 02:29 UTC). Customer uses strict egress allowlist. Repro steps + logs below.

maya: we started seeing 503s and SDK errors at ~02:29. Only internal traffic to the endpoint affected, public hosted customers fine. We have a NAT with outbound restrictions.

jamie: TL;DR hypothesis: rotation uploaded a chain that contains both the old cross-signed intermediate and the new intermediate (they are cross-signed). Some TLS stacks (Go) pick the wrong path from the bundle and fail if they can't fetch missing intermediate via AIA/OCSP (egress blocked).

ryan: can you paste the openssl s_client output? that'll show the chain order.

jamie: here — ran from a repro host inside the customer's VPC (no egress allowed):
```
openssl s_client -connect acme-private.example:443 -servername acme-private.example -showcerts 
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = ExampleRoot, CN = ExampleRootCA
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=acme-private.example
   i:/CN=CrossSigned-Int
 1 s:/CN=CrossSigned-Int
   i:/CN=New-Int
 2 s:/CN=New-Int
   i:/C=US, O=ExampleRoot, CN=ExampleRootCA
---
```

jamie: note chain contains both CrossSigned-Int and New-Int in that order. If the verifier tries path leaf->CrossSigned-Int->?? and cannot reach the cross-signed issuer (AIA) it can fail.

maya: confirming customer cannot reach external AIA/OCSP endpoints by policy. They allow only a short list of IPs (no public OCSP).

li: rotator logs? maybe we pushed both intermediates into fullchain. if both exist and share subject name, some clients will build the wrong path.

jamie: rotator-bot notification attached earlier: 
```
rotator-bot: rotation job 2026-03-16T02:25Z finished for cert-id=cert-789; uploaded fullchain.pem (4 certs), leaf + CrossSigned-Int + New-Int + root
```

jamie: rotator uploaded both intermediates intact. we also see an extra cross-signed cert that has same subject as New-Int but different issuer (cross-signed by old CA).

ryan: Go's crypto/x509 path builder is sensitive to available intermediate candidates and will sometimes prefer a chain that requires fetching AIA to complete. If egress blocked, verification fails with 'x509: certificate signed by unknown authority'. Openssl often builds a different path and succeeds. Explains why some SDKs fail, others don't.

alex: short term workaround for customer: upload a canonicalized fullchain that contains only leaf -> New-Int -> root (remove CrossSigned-Int), or temporarily open egress to the AIA/OCSP endpoints. Which is easier for them?

maya: they prefer to avoid opening egress. can we accept an uploaded fixed fullchain on their Private control plane?

jamie: yes. support can accept an uploaded PEM for the endpoint — steps: 1) export leaf + canonical intermediates in correct order (leaf first), 2) upload via support portal (link: https://support.redwood.ai/private-upload), or we can patch on our side if ops approves.

li: longer-term fix: rotator should dedupe and canonicalize chain when cross-signed intermediates exist. algorithm: pick intermediates by matching Issuer->Subject edges and prefer the path that doesn't require external AIA fetches (i.e., prefer signer chain present in bundle). Also remove duplicates by SKI/AKI. I'll open a PR.

ryan: agreed. also add a check in rollout to detect cross-signed duplicates and warn to prevent customer impact.

jamie: quick runnable repro for engineers (inside VPC without egress):
```
# from a repro host inside customer VPC
curl -v https://acme-private.example/health --resolve acme-private.example:443:10.20.30.40
# or to inspect chain
openssl s_client -connect acme-private.example:443 -servername acme-private.example -showcerts | sed -n '1,120p'
```

jamie: logs show these client errors in our LB logs: `tls: handshake failure from 10.20.30.50: remote error: unknown_ca`

maya: ack, customer will: 1) upload canonical fullchain, 2) run canary traffic. they'll message when done.

alex: patch proposal: dedupe by SKI and reorder by issuer chain; fallback: if multiple chains possible, prefer the chain where every issuer is present in the uploaded bundle (no AIA required). I'll draft RFC.

li: opened internal issue INF-2142 with rotator logs + repro links. tagging @ryan for verifier notes.

ryan: reading. thanks. I'll add unit tests for chain canonicalization and a small integration test that simulates egress-blocked clients.

jamie: thanks all. action items: support to collect uploaded fullchain from customer, ops to apply temporary patch if needed, infra to land rotator dedupe RFC. :eyes: :+1:

rotator-bot: run-id=rot-20260316-0224, config=canonicalize=false (current)

jamie: re: rotator config — leaving canonicalize=false was the immediate trigger. we should flip to true once tests land.

maya: will update when upload complete. thanks team. :pray:
